DL10CT 1190 respectively (hereinafter refereed to as 'vehicle in question').

My issue-wise findings are as under:-
 ISSUE No.1:
Whether injured / petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 21.05.2021 at 7.30 p.m. at Ram Murti Pasi Marg between Gate No.2 & 3, near Adventure sports Mall Sec-11, Rohini,
Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle i.e. car bearing registration no. DL10CT 1190 by respondent no. 1 (Dalbir Singh)? OPP.
Onus to

prove this issue was upon the petitioner and to prove that she has suffered injuries in this accident on account of rash and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1, petitioner examined herself as PW1 and tendered her evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A.

PW1/petitioner in her evidence affidavit deposed that on 21.05.2021 at about 07.30 P.M. she was sitting in e-rickshaw bearing no. DL-11EA-3518 along with her husband Jugnu (injured in connected case), as a passenger and were going to their residence Kirari, Suleman Nagar from E.S.I. Hospital Sector 15,
Rohini after meeting their neighbour /patient Madhu who was admitted in the E.S.I. Hospital and Kishor Paswan (injured in another connected case) was driving the said e-rickshaw very carefully at normal speed by following all traffic rules and regulations on extreme left side of the road and when e-rickshaw reached at Rammurti Passi Marg, Sector-11 Rohini, between gate no. 2 and 3, Adventure Sports Mall, suddenly a car bearing registration No. DL10CT 1190 came from back side in rash,
negligent and zigzag manner with uncontrolled high speed and without following the traffic norms first hit our E-rickshaw from back side by its front left side then a green colour three wheeler goods carrier bearing no. DL-ILZ-4871 and thereafter hit a pedestrian with great impact.

PW1 further deposed that the impact was so powerful that E-rickshaw and three wheeler goods carrier both overturned and they all sustained grievous injuries and they were immediately removed to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, Pitampura for treatment.
PW1 further deposed that the accident took place due to sole rash, negligent and zigzag driving and high speed by the driver / respondent no. 1 of the car bearing No. DL10CT 1190.

Nothing material has come on record to disbelieve the testimony of PW1/petitioner, as far as negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 is concerned, as being injured, petitioner is natural eye-witness of accident and respondent no. 1 has not at all cross examined the PW1.

Further, respondent no. 1,
being driver of offending vehicle was himself material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances and manner, the accident has taken place but he opted not to enter into the witness box and did not lead any evidence.

Further, there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case, meaning thereby that respondent no. 1 has nothing to say about the rash and negligence on his part and the manner in which the accident had occurred as deposed by the PW1.
Further, the DAR shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/337/338 IPC.
Apart from deposition of PW1 / petitioner, the fact that she suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by her MLC filed along with DAR.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.

Further, relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under:-
"The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.

sentences.text: This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.
The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".

Considering all this, it stands proved that Laxmi Vs. Dalbir Singh &

10.

As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured,
petitioner is the natural eye-witness of accident and is well within her rights to claim compensation from the respondents.
Accordingly, the question of right of the injured for claiming of compensation is decided in favour of the petitioner.

Now, the second part of the issue in hand with respect to the quantum of compensation is to be adjudicated and below are the finding: -
11.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009),
held as under: -
"Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

In the light of the above discussion, the aspect of liability of the respondents is to be adjudicated and findings are mentioned below: -
17.
Admittedly, the vehicle was insured.
However, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has taken certain technical defence and has not filed any legal offer.

However, as stated above, one of the connected case has already been settled by the Ins. Co., which inter- alia means that Ins. Co. has no statutory defence and hence, merely taking technial pleas, that too without any supporting evidence, insurnce company cannot escape from its liabilities.

In view of the above discussion, since the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner /
insured and to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Issue no. 2 is accordingly decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co.
holding that petitioner is entitled to get award amount as compensation from respondent no.3 / Ins.
Co.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under:-
"The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.
This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.
The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".
As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured,
petitioner is the natural eye-witness of accident and is well within her rights to claim compensation from the respondents.
Accordingly, the question of right of the injured for claiming of compensation is decided in favour of the petitioner.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.
Though, there is no documentary evidence except deposition of petitioner that she has incurred amount towards special diet, conveyance etc.
However, seeing nature of injuries suffered by petitioner, it is presumed that petitioner must have incurred some amount towards special diet for her speedy recovery and also to go and fro to hospital and hence a sum of Rs.20,000/- each towards special diet and conveyance awarded to the petitioner.
13.
In this regard though not quoted, reliance is placed upon Kirti & Anr. Etc.
v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited in Civil Appeal Nos.1920/2021, Rajendra Singh v. National Insurance Company Limited in Civil Appeal Nos.2624/2020 and law laid down by Hon'ble Gauhati High Court in Sri Mrinal Kanti Debnath & Ors. v.
United India Insurance Company Limited & Ors.
Accordingly, in view of the above judgment, petitioner is entitled to get compensation towards loss to future income, on the basis of Minimum Wages Act applicable in the State of Delhi for skilled worker, which were Rs. 19,291/- per month, prevalent at the time of accident.
14. As far as loss of income during the treatment is concerned, as stated above petitioner has suffered 45% permanent disability in relation to right lower limb and considering the same and long treatment of petitioner, it is presumed that petitioner would have not been able to continue her work for about 6 months.
15. As far as compensation on account of loss to future income on account of permanent disability is concerned, it is a matter of record that during the pendency of the case, petitioner was referred to Satyawadi Raja Harishchandra Hospital, Narela, Delhi for assessment of permanent disability and a certificate received on record as per which, the petitioner has suffered 45% permanent disability in relation to her right lower limb, which is not likely to improve.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that petitioner has suffered 45% permanent disability in relation to right lower limb and following the principles of justice, equity and good conscience and to adopt more realistic, pragmatic and liberal approach, the tribunal is of the view that such kind of disability would definitely hamper day to day activity and household work throughout the entire life of petitioner.
Hence, functional disability /
percentage of loss of earning capacity in relation to disability is taken as 22.5% qua whole body.
As per Aadhar card of petitioner, her birth years is 1999 which inter alias means that petitioner was 22 years in age at the time of accident and as per judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, of Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioner is also entitled to get 40% of enhancement of salary, as she was below 40 years in age at the time of accident.
No tax is deducted since the said income of petitioner is not taxable.
However, as stated above, one of the connected case has already been settled by the Ins. Co., which inter- alia means that Ins. Co. has no statutory defence and hence, merely taking technial pleas, that too without any supporting evidence, insurnce company cannot escape from its liabilities.
In view of the above discussion, since the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner /
insured and to pay compensation to the petitioner.
